newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks tumble at open.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks tumble at open.

text.p: European stock markets opened sharply lower on Monday after Wall Street suffered its second biggest points loss in history on Friday.
However, some prices bounced off their lows amid uncertainty over whether the drop marked an end to the long bull run on European and U.S. stock markets or a temporary correction to the upward trend.
A weak dollar and worries about U.S. profits wiped 247.37 points, or more than three percent, off the Dow Jones Industrial Average to 7,694.66 on Friday.
Wall Street's fall prompted heavy selling on Monday on Asian markets, many of which are also being undermined by currency turmoil in the region.
Continental European markets, many of which were closed on Friday for a holiday, generally suffered more than London, which had already reacted to the early stages of the Dow plunge.
But London still had a tough start to the week, with the FTSE 100 index of blue chips down 58.1 points or 1.19 percent at 4,807.7 after half an hour's trade.

This marked a recovery from levels in pre-market trading and so far was short of dealers' forecasts before the market opened that the blue chip index would lose up to 1.6 percent. The FTSE tumbled 2.5 percent on Friday, its largest loss in percentage terms in five years.
Analysts said Monday's initial sell-off might be met with some caution as the U.S. bond market did not fall on Friday and investors were given the weekend to assess the market's condition.

"I think what will happen is that the market-makers will mark it down quickly, and then there will be a pause for the investor reaction and that will determine the next move," Richard Jeffrey, head of research at Charterhouse Tilney, said before the market opened.
London would also wait for direction from Wall Street when it reopened but fears that British interest rates might have to rise again during the rest of the year would weigh on shares, he said.
Some traders said the FTSE 100 could fall even further as it caught up with the Dow drop, which reverberated on Asian markets. The 225-share Nikkei average in Tokyo fell 1.47 percent on Monday.
German shares dropped sharply in pre-bourse electronic trading. The IBIS DAX index fell as low as 3,965.31, down 2.75 percent from Friday's close of computerised trade.
But then it staged a partial recovery with the IBIS climbing back over 4,000 to 4,005.60, albeit still down 71.99 points or 1.77 percent.
Paris, one of a number of markets closed on Friday for Assumption Day, was particularly hard hit with the CAC-40 down 79.86 points or 2.73 percent at 2,841.98 shortly after the opening.
Italian stocks slid more than 2.5 percent at the start and Spanish stocks 2.69 percent. The Swiss market fell 1.05 percent and Vienna's ATX index lost more than three percent.

On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar remained under pressure against the mark on jitters about German interest rates before the Bundesbank holds its first meeting on Thursday following the summer break.
Markets are also awaiting the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee -- the central bank's policy-making arm -- which meets to consider interest rates on Tuesday.
The dollar remained soft due to the German rate jitters but stayed above 1.81 marks after hitting an 1.8060 overnight low.
